title: Microsoft Copilot app: Chat suggests a better-fit mode such as Cowork
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout details, access rules, licensing and automation are supported. Two minor corrections would complete the route to service-level consumption and cite the reference behind the additional reporting options.

claims.claim: Chat in the Copilot app will suggest a better-fit mode based on the user's prompt, where applicable.
claims.quote: The Chat experience in the Copilot app will suggest a better-fit mode based on the user's prompt, if applicable.

claims.claim: The roadmap names Cowork and other supported modes as they become available.
claims.quote: For example, it will suggest Cowork or other supported modes as they become available.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The suggestion card appears after the user sends a prompt in Chat.
claims.quote: Users will see a suggestion card after they send a prompt in Chat

claims.claim: The card explains the better-fit mode.
claims.quote: with an explanation of the better-fit mode

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Switching to the suggested mode is the user's choice.
claims.quote: an option for the user to switch to the suggested mode

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Chat conversation is attached to the prompt in the new mode to maintain context.
claims.quote: Their chat conversation will be attached to the prompt in the new mode to maintain context.

claims.claim: The notice describes a banner offering a switch or remaining in Chat.
claims.quote: In the banner, the user will see an option to switch to the suggested experience (ie. Cowork) or remain in Chat.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Switching takes the user directly to the suggested experience with the prompt already sent.
claims.quote: If the user selects the option to switch, they will be brought directly to the suggested experience with the prompt already sent, along with the context from their Chat conversation attached.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationales
claims.claim: Suggestions appear only for experiences the user can already access, and do not grant new access.
claims.quote: Users will see suggestions only for experiences they can access. For example, users who do not have access to Cowork will not see a suggestion to use Cowork.

claims.claim: MC1536065 was updated on 13 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the Rollout schedule to reflect timing for Standard and Deferred audiences.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not explain the mechanism for deciding which mode fits better.

claims.quote: No admin action is required to prepare for this change.

claims.quote: Consider informing your users and help desk that Copilot may suggest another Copilot mode when that mode may better fit a request or task.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends considering a review of Cowork-granting policy membership and confirming the intended billing configuration.
claims.quote: Consider reviewing which users are included in a spending policy that grants Cowork access, and confirm your intended usage-based billing configuration.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat mode handoffs suggestion card banner disable admin setting Microsoft Graph; "Copilot" "mode" "suggestion" "setting". Opened configure-copilot-admin-center, cowork-admin-governance and cowork-access; no card-specific UI or API found.

claims.claim: Microsoft's usage-based billing page lists a Copilot licence as required for Cowork.
claims.quote: Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.claim: Cowork model responses, tool and skill calls, image generation and browser tasks count towards organisational consumption.
claims.quote: Activities such as model responses, tool and skill calls, image generation, and browser tasks count toward your organization's consumption.

claims.claim: Cowork uses usage-based billing measured in Copilot Credits, supporting the variable cost field.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits. ... Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects Cowork's Copilot licence requirement together with consumption billing.
claims.quote: This model complements fixed subscription licensing with a flexible payment option that aligns to actual usage. ... Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Cowork access is granted through the scope of a spending policy selecting Cowork, which also determines eligibility for Cowork suggestions.
claims.quote: Users in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork can use Cowork.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[2].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Removing Cowork access requires removing the user from every spending policy that includes Cowork.
claims.quote: To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[2].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A low credit limit does not remove Cowork access.
claims.quote: Setting a very low credit limit doesn't prevent access. A user can still open Cowork and start work until the limit is reached.

claims.claim: The old Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents no longer controls who can use Cowork.
claims.quote: The Cowork agent entry is still visible under Agents > All Agents, but any configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork.

claims.claim: Cowork operates within the user's existing permissions and security boundaries.
claims.quote: It connects to your Outlook, Calendar, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and other Microsoft 365 services, operating within your existing permissions and security boundaries.

claims.claim: Cowork carries out multi-step tasks.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Cowork is an AI-powered agentic system that carries out multi-step tasks on your behalf across Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Cowork can send emails.
claims.quote: Cowork executes it—sending emails, scheduling meetings, creating documents, posting in Teams, conducting research, and managing files.

claims.claim: Cowork can schedule meetings.
claims.quote: Cowork executes it—sending emails, scheduling meetings, creating documents, posting in Teams, conducting research, and managing files.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes sensitive Cowork actions as requiring explicit user approval.
claims.quote: Each action is visible in the conversation, and sensitive actions require your explicit approval before they're executed.

claims.claim: The Auto-apply new services toggle is selected by default for spending policies.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services automatically adds newly supported services while enabled and does not add them automatically when disabled.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy. When the setting is off, future services and agents aren't automatically included.

claims.claim: Precedence between overlapping Cowork policies chooses the applicable limits rather than whether access is granted.
claims.quote: When a user is in multiple policies that select Cowork, the precedence rules only choose which limits apply—they don't decide whether access is granted.

claims.claim: A more restrictive policy does not override a more permissive Cowork access grant.
claims.quote: Access is decided per service by whether any applicable policy selects that service. A more restrictive policy doesn't override a more permissive one.

claims.claim: The cited Microsoft Graph cost management operations are beta APIs subject to change.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The printed Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity > Scope user and group > Specific groups > group > Select agents and services > Cowork path creates a group-scoped Cowork policy.
claims.quote: On the Scope user and group step, choose Specific groups and select the security group. ... On the Select agents and services step, select Cowork.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings/{serviceId} changes a policy's service access setting.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b/serviceSettings/cowork

claims.claim: The service-setting request body sets state, and the reference example disables serviceId cowork.
claims.quote: The state property can be updated. ... "state": "disabled" ... "serviceId": "cowork"

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The policy workflow starts at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy and uses Identity scope for users or groups.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy. ... Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope. Use this option when you need to manage usage by users or groups for a supported service.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Spending limits reaches policy credit-limit settings.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... The spending policy details fly-out opens ... Spending limits

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates spending-policy limits.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b

claims.claim: The spending-policy PATCH body can set periodLimit.

claims.claim: The spending-policy PATCH body can set perUserLimit.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption in the Microsoft 365 admin center is the reporting surface for Cowork service consumption.
claims.quote: Select the Consumption tab. ... The Policies view is the default view ... In the Agents and services view, review usage for supported services. For example, Cowork and Work IQ API.
claims.fix: Complete controls[3].ui.path and the corresponding monitoring instruction as 'Copilot > Cost Management > Consumption > Agents and services'; the printed path stops on the right page, whose default view is Policies. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending.

claims.claim: GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageDetails/{userId}/services retrieves one user's service-level credit consumption.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/usageReports/userUsageDetails/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/services?startDateTime=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z&endDateTime=2026-07-02T00:00:00Z

claims.claim: This reporting operation splits one user's consumption by governed service for a timestamp window.
claims.quote: objects that split one user's raw consumption of Copilot Credits by governed service for a timestamp window.

claims.claim: Learn lists further API usage reports by group, service and funding class.
claims.quote: usage reports that break down consumption by user, security group, governed service, and funding class.
